text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The voter registration exercise in Tana River district has not yet taken off due to lack of transport to the area.
- The opposition FORD-Asili party is faced with imminent collapse unless its two leaders Kenneth Matiba and Martin Shikuku are disciplined.
- Mwai Kibaki, chairman of the opposition Democratic party, says only two days are needed for constitutional reforms demanded by the opposition and religious organisations.
- Pressure mounts on opposition leader Martin Shikuku over his saying at the weekend he would support President Daniel arap Moi "if need be" to deny Matiba a chance of winning the presidency.
- At least 60 suspects escape while being transported to a government prison in Eldoret in the Rift Valley.
- Five people were killed and two reported missing in ethnic clashes in Isiolo district.

- The secretary-general of the ruling Kenya African National Union party condemns the church for its uncompromising stand over constitutional change and says reforms are only possible after the general election.
- The Supreme Council of Kenya Moslems distances itself from a call by religious bodies for immediate constitutional reforms.
- Opposition alliance activists are named as masterminds behind a strike by "matatu" minibus taxis that paralysed public transport in Nairobi on Monday. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
